title: GPU queue simulator and cost-fuzzing labbook
content:
Goal: Rapidly iterate on scheduling policies, batching heuristics, and pricing assumptions to estimate per-token cost and tail-latency risk for different tenant mixes. This is a personal labbook / scratchpad for the prototype simulator and a set of cost-fuzzing experiments. Not final; lots of TODOs and rough edges.

High-level motivation:
- We need a lightweight, configurable simulator that models: GPU device queues, batching formation, preemption/backfill, KV cache warmup, and spot vs reserved capacity economics.
- Use it to answer questions like: how much tail-latency is introduced by aggressive batching at 95th/99th percentiles across tenant mixes? How do reserved commitments of different sizes reduce unit cost under realistic bursty traffic?

Design constraints and scope:
- Fast to run (seconds to minutes for large traces) — favor discrete-event simulation (DES) over full microsecond-level emulation.
- Pluggable workload generators and simple device models (A100-40GB, A100-80GB, H100) with throughput profiles keyed by model family and sequence length distribution.
- Configurable batching policy primitives: max_batch_size, batch_timeout_ms, prefer_short_requests, size_based_prioritization, tenant_priority.
- Economic model: per-hour cost (reserved vs spot), preemption penalty (recovery time + lost tokens), and amortized infra overhead.

Simulator component sketch (ASCII):

  +-----------------+     +-----------------+     +-----------------+
  | Workload Gen    | --> | Ingress Broker  | --> | Device Pools    |
  | (profiles/traces)|     | (queue + rules) |     | (GPU+Batcher)   |
  +-----------------+     +-----------------+     +-----------------+
                                   |                    |
                                   v                    v
                              +------------+       +-------------+
                              | Scheduler  |<----->| KV Warmup   |
                              | (policies) |       | cache model  |
                              +------------+       +-------------+

Key models and simplifications:
- Request model: {tenant_id, model_id, seq_len, token_count, is_streaming, arrival_time, max_latency_ms}
- Device model: fixed throughput per token (tokens/sec) as a function of model variant and batch size; slot count per GPU; simplified memory model only to decide if KV cache warmup is needed (hit after X tokens).
- Batching: continuous-batching simulation where arrival events are added to an open batch until max_batch_size or batch_timeout triggers. Batches then consume a device slot for duration = tokens_in_batch / effective_throughput(batch_size, model).
- Preemption/backfill: two priority classes (reserved, spot). Spot can be preempted with a configurable drain_time and penalty_rate (fraction of in-flight tokens lost).

API / config sketch (stringified YAML-ish):

sim:
  seed: 42
  duration_seconds: 7200
  time_resolution_ms: 1
devices:
  - name: a100-40
    gpus: 8
    throughput_profile:
      gpt2-small:
        base_tps: 80000   # tokens per second at batch_size 1
        batch_scaling_curve: "logistic( max_efficiency=0.95, k=0.02 )"
  - name: h100
    gpus: 4
    throughput_profile:
      gpt3-medium:
        base_tps: 160000
workloads:
  - name: synthetic-chatty
    mix:
      - model: gpt3-medium
        percent: 60
        seq_len_dist: "poisson(lambda=40)"
      - model: gpt2-small
        percent: 40
        seq_len_dist: "pareto(alpha=1.5, scale=16)"
ingress:
  queue_policy: multi-priority
  priorities:
    - name: reserved
      weight: 1.0
    - name: spot
      weight: 0.5
batching:
  max_batch_size: 64
  batch_timeout_ms: 10
  prefer_short_requests: true
economics:
  reserved_hourly: 7.2   # $/GPU-hour
  spot_hourly: 1.8
  preemption_penalty_seconds: 12
  amortized_overhead: 0.12

Simulator API endpoints (for running experiments):
- /simulate/run with body {config_id, scenario_overrides} -> returns metrics summary id
- /simulate/trace-export?trace_id=... -> zipped event trace with compact events
- /simulate/compare?baseline=...&variant=... -> diff of aggregated metrics

Output metrics (to collect):
- per-tenant: p50/p95/p99 latency (enqueue + service), tokens_per_second, effective_cost_per_1e6_tokens (including amortized overhead)
- queue metrics: average queue length, fraction of batches > 32, average batch_size
- device utilization: per-GPU busy_fraction over time, tail busy spikes
- preemption stats: preemption_count, tokens_lost, reclaim_time_distribution
- economic KPIs: total_cost, wasted_cost_due_to_preemption, reserved_savings_vs_spot

Experiment matrix (ideas):
1) Baseline small tenants: 500 tenants, uniform low qps, default batching. Measure p99 with different reserved ratios (0%, 30%, 70%).
2) Bursty tenant mixes: 50 heavy tenants (spiky), 450 light ones. Vary batch_timeout_ms (5, 10, 20) and max_batch_size (32, 64, 128).
3) Aggressive batching + prefer_short_requests toggled: see effect on short tail latency and cost per token for short requests.
4) Preemption stress test: 40% spot footprint with periodic preemption waves; measure lost tokens and cost after applying penalty amortization.
5) KV warmup cold-start effect: introduce new tenants at t=0 who have empty KV caches; simulate warmup hits after X tokens and track latency spike windows.

Quick notes on calibration sources / data: 
- Use production ingress histograms (per-model seq_len, per-tenant qps) for synthetic workload seeding — ask ENG observability for sample histograms (ticket linked above).
- Throughput profiles: start with microbenchmarks we have in perf repo (links TODO) and parameterize batch scaling curve from empirical data.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we model KV cache eviction at per-model granularity or per-tenant? Lightweight first: per-tenant boolean warm/cold window.
- How to fold function/tool-calling (sync external API O call) into batch modeling? For now treat as added per-request latency fudge factor.
- Support for streaming responses (token-incremental eligibility for batching) — needs specialized event model; postpone to v2.
- Validate simulator accuracy vs small-scale A/B deployments (run controlled experiment on a 4-GPU pool and compare).

Experiment tracking conventions (personal):
- name experiments with pattern: sim.YYYYMMDD.short-desc (e.g., sim.20250122.reserved-30-batch10)
- store runs in /sim-results/<config-hash>/run-<timestamp>.csv and attach config.yaml used
- capture random seed in metadata and retain raw event trace for preemption debugging

Notes from quick prototype run (2025-01-20):
- With max_batch_size:64 and batch_timeout_ms:10 on an a100-40 profile, p99 for short-seq-heavy mix climbed to 850ms vs 160ms baseline (unbatched), cost reduced 32% (tokens per $ up).
- Prefer_short_requests=true reduced p99 to ~520ms but increased average cost by ~4% due to less batching efficiency.
- Preemption waves (simulated) show >15% of spot tokens lost when preemption_penalty_seconds=12; amortized cost impact depends heavily on reclaim latency distribution.

Immediate next steps (for me):
- Flesh out throughput_profile format and wire to perf microbench outputs.
- Implement multi-priority DES core (priority queue with preemption hooks).
- Add calibration harness to compare sim output to small cluster job logs.
- Write quick notebook to visualize batch-size distribution over time and correlate with latency spikes.

Random implementation scribbles (pseudo-code for batch formation):

function tryFormBatch(priority_queue, now):
  batch = []
  start = now
  while len(batch) < cfg.max_batch_size and (now - start) < cfg.batch_timeout_ms:
    req = priority_queue.peek()
    if req is None: break
    if cfg.prefer_short_requests and req.seq_len < short_threshold and len(batch) + req.token_count <= cfg.max_batch_size:
      batch.append(priority_queue.pop_shortest())
    else:
      batch.append(priority_queue.pop())
  if len(batch) == 0: return None
  return Batch(batch, formed_at=now)

Wrap-up: This is a scratchpad, expect to iterate quickly. I want to keep experiments reproducible and configs compact. If this proves useful we should move the cleaned spec into a shared repo under eng/serving-runtime/sim/ and add a small web UI for comparing runs.

Contact: maya@redwood.ai (notes personal).

Offhand references to dig up later: perf repo microbenchmarks, billing model spreadsheet (finance), ingress histograms (observability), and JIRA-RI-1423 (linked above).
